text: The Moon's average distance from Earth is about 384,400 kilometres.
as_written: about three hundred eighty-four thousand kilometres away
source: NASA Moon Fact Sheet (NSSDCA)

text: Light takes about 1.28 seconds to travel from the Moon to Earth, so a round trip takes about 2.56 seconds.
as_written: about one point three seconds; At about two point five six seconds
source: NASA Moon Fact Sheet; Lunar Laser Ranging literature (Murphy 2013, Reports on Progress in Physics)

text: A typical laser pointer beam diverges by about one milliradian, giving a spot roughly 384 km across at the Moon's distance. This is distance multiplied by divergence angle, a typical pointer specification and an assumption stated in the narration.
as_written: about a milliradian, which means one metre of width for every kilometre; a spot roughly three hundred eighty-four kilometres across
source: Standard geometric beam-divergence calculation using typical laser pointer manufacturer specifications; distance from NASA Moon Fact Sheet

text: The Moon's diameter is about 3,474 km.
as_written: about three thousand four hundred seventy-four kilometres wide
source: NASA Moon Fact Sheet (NSSDCA)

text: The spot would cover about one ninth of the Moon's diameter.
as_written: about one ninth of its diameter
source: Calculation: 384 km divided by 3,474 km

text: The Moon's apparent angular size in the sky is about half a degree.
as_written: only about half a degree wide
source: NASA Moon Fact Sheet; standard astronomical reference value (about 0.52 degrees mean)

text: The common legal limit for visible laser pointers is five milliwatts.
as_written: limited to five milliwatts
source: US FDA laser product regulations and IEC 60825-1 Class 3R limit

text: Assuming about four billion pointers on the Moon-facing half of Earth at five milliwatts each gives 20 megawatts.
as_written: Four billion pointers at five milliwatts each makes twenty million watts. Twenty megawatts.
source: Calculation: 4 billion x 5 mW; world population over 8 billion per UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs, World Population Prospects 2022

text: The world population passed 8 billion in November 2022, and roughly half the planet faces the Moon at a given time.
as_written: Roughly half the planet is always facing away from the Moon; eight billion people
source: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, World Population Prospects 2022; basic geometry

text: The Moon reflects only about 12 percent of the sunlight that strikes it.
as_written: reflects only about twelve percent of the light that strikes it
source: NASA Moon Fact Sheet (geometric albedo 0.12)

text: Sunlight at the Moon's distance delivers about 1,360 watts per square metre.
as_written: about thirteen hundred sixty watts for every square metre
source: Total Solar Irradiance measurements, NASA SORCE/TIM mission

text: A 384 km wide spot has an area of about 115,000 square kilometres.
as_written: that spot of about one hundred fifteen thousand square kilometres
source: Calculation: pi x (192 km) squared

text: Twenty megawatts spread over that area gives about one ten-thousandth of a watt per square metre, about one eight-millionth of sunlight.
as_written: about one ten-thousandth of a watt; about one eight-millionth
source: Calculation: 20 MW divided by 1.16e11 square metres, compared with 1,361 W per square metre

text: The US FAA recorded more than 13,000 laser incidents involving aircraft in 2023.
as_written: In 2023 the United States Federal Aviation Administration recorded more than thirteen thousand laser incidents
source: US Federal Aviation Administration, Laser Incidents annual statistics, 2023

text: The Earth rotates at fifteen degrees per hour.
as_written: The Earth turns at fifteen degrees every hour
source: Standard astronomy: 360 degrees in 24 hours

text: The Moon rises about fifty minutes later each day.
as_written: the Moon rises about fifty minutes later each night
source: NASA Moon observation guidance; lunar orbital mechanics

text: The cycle of lunar phases takes about 29.5 days.
as_written: about twenty-nine and a half days
source: NASA Moon Fact Sheet (synodic period 29.53 days)

text: Light exerts a force equal to power divided by the speed of light; 20 MW gives about 0.07 newtons, roughly the weight of about seven grams.
as_written: about seven hundredths of a newton; roughly seven grams
source: Radiation pressure physics, calculation 20e6 W / 3e8 m/s; speed of light defined by SI

text: The Moon's mass is about 7.35 times ten to the 22nd kilograms.
as_written: seven point three five followed by twenty-two zeros
source: NASA Moon Fact Sheet (NSSDCA)

text: Applying that force for a year displaces the Moon by about half a nanometre.
as_written: less than a billionth of a metre. About half a nanometre
source: Calculation: x = 0.5 x (F/M) x t squared for one year, F about 0.067 N, M = 7.35e22 kg

text: The Moon recedes from Earth at about 3.8 centimetres per year.
as_written: about three point eight centimetres every year
source: Lunar Laser Ranging data; NASA; Williams, Boggs et al. analyses

text: The Moon's recession is caused by tidal interaction with Earth.
as_written: It is caused by tides
source: NASA / standard tidal dynamics; confirmed by Lunar Laser Ranging

text: Apollo 11 astronauts placed a retroreflector array of 100 corner cubes in July 1969.
as_written: In July of 1969 ... one hundred of them
source: NASA Apollo 11 Lunar Surface Experiments Package documentation; Lunar Laser Ranging Experiment

text: Apollo 14 left an array of 100 corner cubes and Apollo 15 left an array of 300.
as_written: Apollo 14 added another array of one hundred. Apollo 15 left one with three hundred.
source: NASA Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments; International Laser Ranging Service

text: The Soviet Union landed laser reflectors on its Lunokhod robotic rovers.
as_written: The Soviet Union also landed reflectors on its robotic rovers
source: International Laser Ranging Service; Soviet Lunokhod 1 and 2 missions

text: Lunar laser ranging measures the Earth-Moon distance to about a millimetre.
as_written: to about a millimetre
source: Murphy 2013, Lunar laser ranging: the millimeter challenge, Reports on Progress in Physics; APOLLO project at Apache Point Observatory

text: Lunar laser ranging revealed evidence of a fluid lunar core.
as_written: evidence that the Moon has a fluid core
source: Williams, Boggs, Yoder, Ratcliff, Dickey 2001, Journal of Geophysical Research: Planets

text: Lunar laser ranging has tested the equivalence principle for Earth and Moon falling toward the Sun to roughly a part in ten trillion.
as_written: to within roughly a part in ten trillion
source: Williams, Turyshev and Boggs 2012, Classical and Quantum Gravity

text: The Moon is estimated to be about 4.5 billion years old.
as_written: four and a half billion years
source: NASA Moon science; lunar sample radiometric dating

text: Extrapolating the present recession rate backwards is inconsistent with the Moon's age, so the rate must have varied; its history is debated.
as_written: The numbers do not fit. So the rate must have changed over time ... Researchers disagree about the history
source: Bills and Ray 1999 Geophysical Research Letters; Green et al. 2017 Proceedings of the Royal Society A on tidal evolution

text: A 5 milliwatt green 532 nanometre laser emits about 13 quadrillion photons per second.
as_written: about thirteen quadrillion photons every second
source: Calculation: 5e-3 W divided by photon energy hc/lambda of about 3.7e-19 J at 532 nm
